summary: DLMF 4.24 Inverse Trigonometric Functions: Further Properties: which requires z (=x+iy) to lie between the two rectangular hyperbolas given by
body: NIST DLMF section 4.24 (Inverse Trigonometric Functions: Further Properties) says: "which requires z (=x+iy) to lie between the two rectangular hyperbolas given by The above equations are interpreted in the sense that every value of the left-hand side is a value of the right-hand side and vice versa. All square roots have either possible value." Equation 4.24.1 on the page has alt text "\operatorname{arcsin}z=z+\frac{1}{2}\frac{z^{3}}{3}+\frac{1\cdot 3}{2\cdot 4}% \frac{z^{5}}{5}+\frac{1\cdot 3\cdot 5}{2\cdot 4\cdot 6}\frac{z^{7}}{7}+\cdots,". Equation 4.24.2 on the page has alt text "\operatorname{arccos}z=(2(1-z))^{1/2}\*\left(1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1\cdot 3% \cdot 5\cdots(2n-1)}{2^{2n}(2n+1)n!}(1-z)^{n}\right),". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
